description: A company that designs chips and sells them under its own name, or designs them for its own products. It is the 'seller' counted in the headline chip-market statistics.
name: Chip company (category)

description: A chip company that designs its chips and also makes, packages and tests them in its own factories.
name: Integrated device manufacturer (IDM) (category)

description: An IDM that makes commodity-like memory chips (DRAM, NAND flash, HBM); prices swing hard with the cycle and are set in periodically renegotiated agreements.
name: Memory chip maker (category)

description: A chip company that designs and sells chips but owns no fab; it pays foundries to make wafers and OSATs to package and test them.
name: Fabless chip company (category)

description: A cloud provider or device maker that designs custom chips for its own products or data centres (e.g. hyperscaler CPUs and AI chips) rather than for sale on the open market.
name: System company designing its own chips (category)

description: A company that supplies what chip designers need to design: software, licensed design blocks or design services.
name: Design-enablement provider (category)

description: Sells electronic design automation (EDA) software used to design and verify chips, mostly as time-based licences.
name: EDA vendor (category)

description: Licenses reusable, pre-designed chip blocks (e.g. processor cores, interfaces) for a licence fee and often a royalty on every chip shipped.
name: Semiconductor IP licensor (category)

description: Takes a customer's chip from specification to finished product, doing design work and managing the foundry and packaging steps (also called a design house or turnkey ASIC provider).
name: Design-service / ASIC house (category)

description: Licenses patents to device makers (not design blocks to chip designers) for a royalty based on the device's selling price.
name: Device-level patent licensor (category)

description: A company that manufactures, packages, tests or makes masks for chips designed by others.
name: Contract manufacturing-service provider (category)

description: A contract chip manufacturer: it makes wafers to its customers' designs using its own processes.
name: Foundry (category)

description: A foundry that only manufactures for customers and does not sell chips of its own design.
name: Pure-play foundry (category)

description: A foundry business run inside a company that also designs and sells its own chips (an IDM offering spare or dedicated capacity to outside customers).
name: IDM foundry business (category)

description: A contractor that cuts, packages and tests chips for IDMs and fabless companies; the customer usually keeps title to the wafers.
name: OSAT (outsourced assembly and test) (category)

description: Makes photomasks (the patterned plates used in lithography) from each customer's design, either as an independent 'merchant' shop or a 'captive' shop inside a chipmaker.
name: Photomask maker (category)

description: A supplier of the tools, materials, chemicals, gases and software that fabs and packaging plants consume.
name: Upstream supplier to fabs (category)

description: Builds the machines used to make and test chips, and earns a large share of revenue from servicing and upgrading its installed base.
name: Semiconductor equipment maker (category)

description: Makes front-end tools: lithography, deposition, etch, implant, polishing (CMP), metrology and inspection.
name: Wafer-fab (front-end) equipment maker (category)

description: Makes automatic test equipment used at wafer probe, final test and system-level test; sells to IDMs, fabless firms, foundries and OSATs.
name: Test-equipment maker (category)

description: Supplies the consumable materials of chipmaking: wafers, photoresists, chemicals, gases, photomask blanks and packaging materials.
name: Semiconductor materials supplier (category)

description: Grows ultra-pure silicon and slices and polishes it into the wafers that chips are built on.
name: Silicon wafer / polysilicon supplier (category)

description: Supplies photoresists, wet chemicals and etchants used in the fab.
name: Process-chemical / photoresist supplier (category)

description: Produces and purifies gases such as neon used in lithography lasers and other process steps.
name: Specialty-gas producer and purifier (category)

description: Makes the substrates (e.g. ABF), lead frames, bonding wire and other materials that chips are packaged with.
name: Packaging-materials / IC-substrate supplier (category)

description: Produces raw minerals such as gallium, germanium or rare earths that are refined into chip materials; production is geographically concentrated.
name: Critical-mineral producer (category)

description: Sells factory software such as manufacturing execution systems (MES), fault detection and yield management to fabs and packaging plants.
name: Manufacturing-software vendor (category)

description: A company that resells chips between chipmakers and buyers.
name: Channel intermediary (category)

description: Buys chips from chipmakers under franchise agreements and resells them to device makers, adding design support, programming and logistics.
name: Authorized (franchised) distributor (category)

description: Resells chips outside the chipmakers' authorized channels (the 'open market'), where provenance is not assured and counterfeits can enter.
name: Independent distributor / broker (category)

description: A company that buys chips to build into products.
name: Chip buyer (category)

description: An original equipment manufacturer that designs and sells end products (computers, phones, cars, industrial equipment) containing chips.
name: OEM / device maker (category)

description: An electronics manufacturing services contractor that assembles chips onto boards and systems for OEMs.
name: EMS provider (category)

description: A party that finances chip companies or fabs (equity, co-investment, loans).
name: Capital provider (category)

description: A financial partner that co-funds a chipmaker's fab construction in exchange for a minority stake in the fab or its output.
name: Financial co-investor in fabs (category)

description: Many transistors and other components built on one piece of semiconductor; about 88% of chip sales.
name: Integrated circuit (IC)

description: Chips that compute or control (processors, accelerators, custom logic); the largest WSTS category.
name: Logic IC

description: Processors built for AI training and inference in data centres; the target of US export controls and the Section 232 tariff.
name: AI accelerator / advanced computing chip

description: Chips that store data (DRAM, NAND flash, HBM and others).
name: Memory IC

description: Dynamic random-access memory: fast working memory, made by a handful of IDMs.
name: DRAM

description: Stacks of DRAM dies joined by through-silicon vias, packaged next to AI processors.
name: High-bandwidth memory (HBM)

description: Non-volatile storage memory, now built in 3D stacks of hundreds of layers.
name: NAND flash

description: Chips that handle real-world signals and power (amplifiers, converters, drivers).
name: Analog IC

description: Microprocessors, microcontrollers and digital signal processors, as grouped by WSTS.
name: Micro IC (MPU/MCU/DSP)

description: Single-function devices such as transistors, diodes and thyristors.
name: Discrete semiconductor

description: Devices that emit or detect light (LEDs, image sensors, laser diodes); excludes LCD panels.
name: Optoelectronics

description: Semiconductor sensors (pressure, motion, magnetic etc.) and actuators.
name: Sensors and actuators

description: PCs, servers and data-centre/AI systems; the largest end use.
name: Computing / AI end market

description: Phones and network equipment.
name: Communications end market

description: Consumer electronics other than PCs and phones.
name: Consumer end market

description: Chips in cars and vehicles.
name: Automotive end market

description: Factory, energy, medical and other industrial equipment.
name: Industrial end market

description: Public-sector and defence uses; WSTS groups military inside Government.
name: Government / military end market

description: University, consortium and company research that precedes product design.
name: Pre-competitive research

description: Specification, logic design, physical design and verification of a chip, using EDA software and licensed IP.
name: Chip design

description: Growing silicon ingots and slicing and polishing them into wafers.
name: Wafer production

description: Turning each finished design into a set of photomasks, one per layer.
name: Mask making

description: Building circuits on wafers in a fab through hundreds of repeated process steps.
name: Wafer fabrication (front end)

description: Testing dies on the wafer, cutting them apart, packaging them and testing again.
name: Assembly, packaging and test (back end)

description: Moving finished chips to buyers, directly or through distributors and the open market.
name: Distribution

description: Mounting chips on boards and building end products (EMS providers and OEMs).
name: System integration

description: Deep-ultraviolet lithography, including immersion DUV (water between lens and wafer); lasers use neon-containing excimer gas.
name: DUV lithography

description: Extreme-ultraviolet lithography at 13.5 nm wavelength using mirrors in vacuum; one supplier makes the scanners; needed at 7 nm and below.
name: EUV lithography (0.33 NA)

description: Next-generation EUV with 0.55 numerical aperture and 8 nm resolution; high-volume use expected from 2027.
name: High-NA EUV lithography (0.55 NA)

description: A 3D fin-shaped transistor introduced in 2011 by Intel; still the mainstream leading-edge transistor before gate-all-around.
name: FinFET transistor

description: Transistor whose gate wraps the channel on all sides; in production at 3 nm/2 nm class; key to scaling below 3 nm.
name: Gate-all-around (nanosheet) transistor

description: Routing power through the back of the wafer to free front-side wiring (e.g. PowerVia, Super Power Rail).
name: Backside power delivery

description: Placing several dies (e.g. a processor and HBM stacks) side by side on a silicon or organic interposer (e.g. CoWoS).
name: 2.5D interposer packaging

description: Stacking dies directly on top of each other with very fine-pitch bonds (e.g. SoIC).
name: 3D stacking and hybrid bonding

description: Building a system from several small dies assembled close together instead of one large chip; improves yield but needs known-good-die testing.
name: Chiplets

description: Glass core substrates proposed to replace organic substrates for large packages (announced, not yet in volume per evidence).
name: Glass package substrates

description: The standard wafer size for advanced fabs; 99.7% of capacity at 45 nm or below.
name: 300 mm silicon wafer

description: A wide-bandgap material used for power and RF chips, now moving to 300 mm wafers.
name: Gallium nitride (GaN) wafers

description: The generational label ('7 nm', '3 nm') attached to a manufacturer's process; not a physical measurement.
name: Process node naming

description: The foundry's rulebook and parts kit for one process: design rules, device models, cell libraries and EDA tech files.
name: Process design kit (PDK)

description: The final geometric layout of a chip handed over at tape-out, in GDSII or OASIS format.
name: Layout database (GDSII / OASIS)

description: The set of photomasks for one design, one per patterned layer.
name: Mask set

description: Electrical test results from test structures on each wafer; one of the few data types foundries routinely share with customers.
name: WAT / PCM data

description: Die-by-die pass/fail (bin) map passed from wafer sort to assembly and final test.
name: Wafer / substrate map

description: Per-lot, per-wafer, per-part test results from testers, commonly in STDF format.
name: Test result data (STDF)

description: Readings from the 100-200 sensors on each process tool, used for fault detection and classification.
name: Equipment sensor data (FDC)

description: Forecasts, orders and allocations exchanged between device makers, chip companies and manufacturers; format and systems not yet evidenced.
name: Demand forecasts and orders

description: Software that runs the fab: tracks lots, WIP, recipes, masks and equipment status, and keeps genealogy.
name: Manufacturing execution system (MES)

description: Software that watches tool sensor data to catch process faults.
name: Fault detection and classification (FDC) system

description: Online system through which a foundry receives tape-outs and gives customers lot status, yield and WAT data (e.g. TSMC-Online).
name: Foundry customer portal

description: The standard for how semiconductor equipment talks to the factory host system.
name: SEMI E30 GEM / SECS

description: Standard data items for wafer and substrate maps from wafer through assembly to final test.
name: SEMI E142 substrate mapping

description: Layout interchange format that succeeded GDSII Stream.
name: SEMI P39 OASIS

description: Common format for semiconductor test results, originated by Teradyne.
name: Standard Test Data Format (STDF)

description: JEDEC memory standard for fourth-generation HBM: up to 2 TB/s and 16-high stacks.
name: JEDEC HBM4 (JESD270-4)

description: Consortium standard for connecting chiplets from different suppliers inside one package.
name: UCIe die-to-die interconnect

description: Monthly and forecast chip sales by product and region compiled from member reports; the source of the headline market size.
name: WSTS world semiconductor market statistics

description: Equipment billings compiled from SEMI and SEAJ member data.
name: SEMI equipment billings statistics

description: Annual semiconductor materials revenue split into fab and packaging materials.
name: SEMI materials market statistics

description: Quarterly revenue of EDA, semiconductor IP and design services.
name: ESD Alliance design-industry revenue

description: UN industry class 'Manufacture of electronic components and boards', wider than chips.
name: ISIC Rev.4 class 2610

description: North American industry 'Semiconductor and other electronic component manufacturing', also wider than chips.
name: NAICS 334410

description: Customs headings for semiconductor devices and integrated circuits.
name: HS headings 8541/8542

description: Multi-year agreements with volume commitments and reserved capacity (foundry) or periodically renegotiated pricing (memory).
name: Long-term capacity / supply agreement

description: Advance payments by customers to reserve foundry capacity or secure supply.
name: Customer capacity prepayment

description: Multi-year licence fees plus a royalty on every chip containing the IP.
name: IP licence fee plus per-chip royalty

description: A percentage of the device's wholesale price, paid quarterly by device makers.
name: Device-level patent royalty

description: Time-based network licences bundled with support, plus some upfront licences and maintenance.
name: EDA time-based licence

description: Supplier agreements that protect distributors against price erosion and obsolescence.
name: Franchised distribution agreement (price protection)

description: Customer keeps title to wafers; no binding volumes; customer bears unused materials.
name: Consigned-wafer OSAT agreement

description: Service, spares and upgrades for installed tools, largely subscriptions.
name: Installed-base service subscription

description: Grants reimbursed on project milestones, loans, investment tax credits with direct pay, and state equity.
name: Milestone-based grant and investment tax credit

description: US Commerce Department bureau that writes and enforces the Export Administration Regulations, including chip and equipment controls and the Entity List.
name: US Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS)

description: Runs the CHIPS Act manufacturing incentives; placed under the US Investment Accelerator in March 2025.
name: CHIPS Program Office (US Commerce / NIST)

description: Administers the Outbound Investment Security Program; the IRS (part of Treasury) administers the 48D credit.
name: US Department of the Treasury

description: Runs Section 301 trade investigations and actions, including on Chinese semiconductors.
name: Office of the US Trade Representative (USTR)

description: Imposes national-security tariffs under Section 232 by proclamation after a Commerce investigation.
name: US President (Section 232 proclamations)

description: Requires Form SD conflict-minerals disclosure from reporting companies.
name: US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)

description: Sued to block Nvidia's acquisition of Arm (abandoned 2022).
name: US Federal Trade Commission (FTC)

description: Defense Microelectronics Activity accreditation of trusted suppliers for sensitive ICs.
name: US DMEA Trusted Supplier Program

description: Proposes EU chip law (Chips Act, Chips Act 2.0), approves State aid and updates the EU dual-use list.
name: European Commission

description: EU agency running the REACH PFAS restriction process; effect on fabs not yet established.
name: European Chemicals Agency (ECHA)

description: Issues the Dutch national export licences for advanced chipmaking equipment.
name: Netherlands Minister for Foreign Trade and Development

description: Controls chipmaking-equipment exports under FEFTA and runs Japan's chip subsidy programme.
name: Japan Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)

description: Licenses critical-mineral exports and runs trade-remedy investigations (e.g. anti-dumping on US analog ICs).
name: China Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM)

description: Conducted the 2023 cybersecurity review of Micron products.
name: China Cybersecurity Review Office (CAC)

description: State-backed equity fund for the chip industry; phase III registered 2024 with CNY 344bn.
name: China National IC Industry Investment Fund (Big Fund)

description: Maintains Taiwan's Strategic High-Tech Commodities entity list.
name: Taiwan MOEA International Trade Administration

description: Passed the K-Chips Act tax-credit amendment (2025) and the Semiconductor Special Act (2026).
name: South Korea National Assembly

description: Runs the Semicon India incentive programme and ISM 2.0.
name: India Semiconductor Mission (MeitY)

description: 42-state regime keeping a common dual-use control list implemented in national law.
name: Wassenaar Arrangement

description: Maintains the ISIC industry classification.
name: UN Statistics Division (ISIC)

description: Non-profit of chip companies that compiles the reference chip-sales statistic from member reports.
name: World Semiconductor Trade Statistics (WSTS)

description: US trade body that publishes WSTS-based monthly sales and value-chain studies.
name: Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA)

description: Global association of equipment and materials suppliers; publishes equipment/materials statistics and runs the SEMI Standards programme.
name: SEMI

description: Contributes member data to SEMI's equipment statistics.
name: Semiconductor Equipment Association of Japan (SEAJ)

description: SEMI technology community that reports electronic system design (EDA and IP) industry revenue.
name: ESD Alliance

description: Founded 1994 to promote the fabless model; renamed 2007.
name: Global Semiconductor Alliance (formerly Fabless Semiconductor Association)

description: Develops open memory, packaging and ESD standards; 380+ members.
name: JEDEC Solid State Technology Association

description: Consortium that maintains the UCIe chiplet interconnect specification.
name: UCIe Consortium

description: US government-industry R&D consortium formed in 1987.
name: SEMATECH

description: Taiwan's state research institute; spun off UMC (1980) and TSMC (1987).
name: Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI)

description: Belgian research centre working on 3D integration, hybrid bonding and chiplets.
name: imec

description: IT research firm that publishes vendor-level worldwide semiconductor revenue estimates (preliminary in January, final around April) that include in-house chips of system companies such as Apple.
name: Gartner, Inc.

description: Market research firm whose semiconductor supply-chain service publishes worldwide semiconductor revenue estimates with a wider (undisclosed) scope than WSTS or Gartner.
name: IDC (International Data Corporation)

description: Research firm (part of Informa TechTarget) that tracks quarterly semiconductor vendor revenue since 2001.
name: Omdia

description: Semiconductor analysis firm that publishes quarterly semiconductor market forecasts with history from 1984 behind platform registration.
name: TechInsights

description: European chip industry body that distributes WSTS data and handles public WSTS inquiries in Europe.
name: European Semiconductor Industry Association (ESIA)

description: Korean chip industry body that handles public WSTS inquiries for Asia Pacific outside Taiwan and China.
name: Korea Semiconductor Industry Association (KSIA)

description: Office in the US Commerce Department created by executive order on 31 March 2025 to speed investments above US$1 billion; it took over the CHIPS Program Office and was tasked with negotiating 'better CHIPS Act deals'.
name: US Investment Accelerator (Department of Commerce)

description: NIST office that manages the US$11 billion CHIPS R&D appropriation (NSTC, advanced packaging programme, Manufacturing USA institute, metrology); since September 2025 it funds R&D mainly through a broad agency announcement that can require equity or royalties.
name: CHIPS Research and Development Office (NIST)

description: Nonprofit incorporated in October 2023 to operate the National Semiconductor Technology Center; received about US$6.3 billion of CHIPS R&D awards by January 2025, but Commerce declared its up-to-US$7.4 billion agreement void in August 2025 and NIST took over the NSTC.
name: Natcast (National Center for the Advancement of Semiconductor Technology)

description: US public-private semiconductor R&D consortium created under the CHIPS Act; operated by Natcast until August 2025 and then brought under direct NIST control, with its three planned facilities (Albany EUV Accelerator, California design facility, Arizona packaging pilot) cancelled.
name: National Semiconductor Technology Center (NSTC)

description: Congressional audit agency required by the FY21 NDAA to report periodically on the CHIPS incentives programme; its December 2025 and August 2026 reports give award, disbursement and cancellation figures.
name: US Government Accountability Office (GAO)

description: Taiwan-based market research firm that publishes quarterly foundry and annual OSAT revenue rankings.
name: TrendForce

description: French market research firm whose advanced-packaging market sizes and wafer splits are the most cited reference for packaging; full reports are paywalled.
name: Yole Group

description: Taiwan-based technology publisher and research unit that estimates global OSAT revenue.
name: DIGITIMES Research

description: US packaging-focused research firm that co-produces the Worldwide Assembly & Test Facility Database with SEMI.
name: TechSearch International

description: Malaysia's government investment-promotion agency for manufacturing, including the semiconductor back end.
name: Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA)

description: Wire-bonded chips in leadframe or laminate packages; lower value, labour-intensive, mostly in China and Southeast Asia.
name: Conventional (wire-bond/leadframe) packaging

description: Bumped die attached face-down to a substrate; the largest advanced-packaging platform by revenue and the base for 2.5D packages.
name: Flip-chip packaging

description: Packaging done on the whole wafer before dicing; fan-in keeps connections within the die, fan-out spreads them into mould compound.
name: Wafer-level packaging (fan-in and fan-out)

description: US agency that investigates dumping and subsidies and issues antidumping and countervailing duty orders (e.g. the 2003 DRAM order on Hynix).
name: US Commerce Department International Trade Administration (Enforcement and Compliance)

description: Government-backed Japanese bank that took preferred shares in Elpida in 2009 under the revised Industrial Revitalization Act.
name: Development Bank of Japan

description: South Korea's central bank; its monthly export price index includes DRAM and flash memory components, one of the few official memory price series.
name: Bank of Korea

description: US computer makers' group (IBM, Tandem, HP and others) founded in 1989 to oppose antidumping measures that raised DRAM prices.
name: Computer Systems Policy Project

aliases: General Administration of Customs of China
description: China's customs agency; co-issues mineral export-control announcements with MOFCOM and enforces licences at the border (no licence, no release). Chinese name: 海关总署.
name: General Administration of Customs of China (GACC)

description: Inter-ministerial mechanism, with its office in MOFCOM, that investigates foreign entities and decides Unreliable Entity List listings and measures. Chinese name: 不可靠实体清单工作机制.
name: China Unreliable Entity List Working Mechanism

description: Provincial chip industry association that petitioned MOFCOM for the 2025 anti-dumping case on US analog chips. Chinese name: 江苏省半导体行业协会.
name: Jiangsu Semiconductor Industry Association

description: MOFCOM bureau that runs China's anti-dumping, anti-discrimination and trade-barrier investigations. Chinese name: 商务部贸易救济调查局、贸易救济局.
name: MOFCOM Trade Remedy and Investigation Bureau

description: SEMI standard defining a constrained OASIS subset used as the input format for mask writing and inspection tools.
name: SEMI P44 OASIS.MASK

description: SEMI standard defining a common job deck format (MALY) that tells mask tools how to place OASIS pattern files on a mask.
name: SEMI P45 MALY job deck format

description: SEMI standard (now Inactive status) for machine-readable photomask orders sent by customers and mask results returned by mask shops.
name: SEMI P10 photomask order data structures

description: A file that instructs a mask writer where and how to place each pattern file (die, test structures, marks) on a mask; formats include MALY, MEBES JB and JEOL JDF.
name: Mask job deck

description: Software that converts signed-off layout into mask-writer data: resolution enhancement/OPC, mask rule checks, fracturing and job decks (e.g. Siemens Calibre MDP, Synopsys MDP).
name: Mask data preparation (MDP) software

description: TSMC's design-ecosystem programme (EDA, IP, Design Center, Value Chain Aggregator, Cloud and 3DFabric alliances) that certifies tools, assesses IP and gives partners early process access.
name: TSMC Open Innovation Platform (OIP)

description: TSMC's minimum quality requirements and scoring for libraries and IP on its processes; scores and usage records are posted on TSMC-Online.
name: TSMC9000 IP assessment programme

description: Samsung Foundry's ecosystem programme of IP, EDA (SAFE-QEDA certification), design-service, cloud and multi-die alliances.
name: Samsung Advanced Foundry Ecosystem (SAFE)

description: Intel Foundry's ecosystem programme (IP, EDA, Design Services, Cloud, USMAG, Value Chain, Chiplet alliances) launched in 2022.
name: Intel Foundry Accelerator Ecosystem Alliance

description: Not-for-profit EDA standards consortium that hosts OpenAccess, distributes LEF/DEF and publishes CMC compact device models.
name: Si2 (Silicon Integration Initiative)

description: Text formats describing cell abstracts/technology (LEF) and placed-and-routed designs (DEF) for place-and-route tools; developed by Cadence, distributed by Si2.
name: LEF/DEF (Library and Design Exchange Formats)

description: Apache-2.0 open process design kit for SkyWater's 130 nm CMOS process, released by Google and SkyWater in 2020.
name: SkyWater SKY130 open-source PDK

description: Apache-2.0 open PDK for GlobalFoundries' 0.18 um MCU process, released with Google (experimental preview).
name: GlobalFoundries GF180MCU open-source PDK

description: Apache-2.0 open PDK for IHP's 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS process, publicly funded in Germany (preview).
name: IHP SG13G2 open-source PDK

description: Intel's 2.5D packaging that embeds small silicon bridges in the organic substrate to link neighbouring dies, instead of a full-size interposer; EMIB-T adds TSVs to the bridge.
name: EMIB (Embedded Multi-die Interconnect Bridge)

description: Intel's family of interposer and 3D die-stacking packages; Foveros Direct uses Cu-Cu hybrid bonding.
name: Foveros

description: Building 2.5D interposers/RDL on large square panels (e.g. 310 mm or 600 mm) instead of 300 mm round wafers to fit more very large packages; in pilot lines at TSMC, ASE and Rapidus in 2026.
name: Panel-level 2.5D packaging (CoPoS and similar)

description: Die-attach step that uses heat and pressure to join micro-bumps die by die; used for HBM DRAM stacking and fine-pitch chip-to-substrate and chip-to-wafer attach in 2.5D packages.
name: Thermo-compression bonding (TCB)

description: French public microelectronics research institute (part of CEA) active in hybrid-bonding research.
name: CEA-Leti

description: Patterning by pressing a mask carrying the circuit pattern into resist on the wafer like a stamp, instead of projecting light through optics; commercialised for chips by Canon (FPA-1200NZ2C).
name: Nanoimprint lithography

description: Lithography using 365 nm light from mercury-vapour lamps; used for larger features, power devices, sensors and packaging. Canon and Nikon sell most i-line units.
name: i-line lithography

description: Deep-UV lithography using 248 nm light from krypton-fluoride excimer lasers; mid-critical layers at mature nodes and in memory.
name: KrF lithography

description: Deep-UV lithography at 193 nm (argon-fluoride lasers) with ultrapure water between lens and wafer to raise the numerical aperture; the workhorse for critical non-EUV layers and multi-patterning.
name: ArF immersion lithography

description: Texas semiconductor consortium (founded 2021, supported by UT Austin) that received Canon's first shipped nanoimprint lithography system.
name: Texas Institute for Electronics

description: San Diego-based electronic-materials advisory firm publishing Critical Materials Reports (CMP, gases, wet chemicals, lithography); public press releases give segment sizes.
name: TECHCET

description: Japanese market research firm whose semiconductor-materials estimates TOK cites for photoresist shares.
name: Fuji Chimera Research Institute

description: SEMI technology community of materials suppliers (substrates, polymers, metals, chemicals, gases) with chapters in America, Korea, Japan and Europe; the Silicon Manufacturers Group (SMG) sits inside it.
name: SEMI Electronic Materials Group (EMG)

description: Fund vehicle that acquired JSR via tender offer through JICC-02, Ltd. in April 2024.
name: JIC Capital (JIC PEFJ1 Limited Partnership)

description: US Commerce Department agency whose Japan semiconductors guide summarises Japanese materials shares.
name: US International Trade Administration (Country Commercial Guides)

description: Georgetown University policy research centre whose open Supply Chain Explorer publishes country and firm market shares per chipmaking tool category, adapted mostly from TechInsights data.
name: Center for Security and Emerging Technology (CSET) / Emerging Technology Observatory

description: Twice-yearly SEMI forecast of equipment sales by segment (WFE, test, A&P), WFE application and region, built from supplier input, WWSEMS and the World Fab Forecast.
name: SEMI Total Semiconductor Equipment Forecast - OEM Perspective

description: SEAJ's fiscal-year series and January/July forecasts of sales by Japanese equipment makers worldwide and of sales into the Japanese market.
name: SEAJ Japanese-made semiconductor equipment sales statistics

description: Multi-year (up to five years at ASML) framework agreement between a tool maker and a chipmaker that sets discounts, credits and free goods; individual tool orders, often with down payments and slot reservations, are drawn against it.
name: Equipment volume purchase agreement

description: Fab-software fee that scales with the customer's wafer manufacturing volumes or data transferred (PDF Solutions Gainshare, secureWISE data, Cimetrix runtime licences), alongside fixed licences and SaaS.
name: Volume-based manufacturing-software fee (Gainshare)

description: The US SEC's public filing system holding 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, 20-F, 6-K and other filings; free keyless JSON/XBRL APIs on data.sec.gov; companies tagged by SIC code.
name: SEC EDGAR (Electronic Data Gathering, Analysis, and Retrieval system)

description: US Standard Industrial Classification code still used by SEC EDGAR to tag filers; covers semiconductor devices incl. solar cells and LEDs; many equipment, materials and EDA firms are coded elsewhere.
name: SIC 3674 Semiconductors and Related Devices

description: Taiwan's official disclosure platform run by TWSE and TPEx under FSC supervision; holds monthly revenue (due before the 10th), quarterly and annual reports and material information; English version e-MOPS. Local-language name(s): 公開資訊觀測站.
name: Market Observation Post System (MOPS)

description: Taiwan's financial regulator; its Securities and Futures Bureau sets what public companies must file on MOPS (Securities and Exchange Act Art. 36). Local-language name(s): 金融監督管理委員會.
name: Financial Supervisory Commission (Taiwan)

description: Official Taiwan exchange industry group for semiconductor companies, assigned on a 50% operating-income rule; 91 TWSE, 111 TPEx and 34 Emerging Stock Board stocks on 2026-10-01. Local-language name(s): 半導體業.
name: TWSE/TPEx industry category 24: Semiconductor Industry

description: Korea's electronic disclosure system run by the Financial Supervisory Service; OpenDART API (key required) returns filings, XML originals, XBRL financials and company industry codes. Local-language name(s): 전자공시시스템.
name: DART (Data Analysis, Retrieval and Transfer System)

description: Korean financial supervisor that operates DART and OpenDART. Local-language name(s): 금융감독원.
name: Financial Supervisory Service (Korea)

description: Japan's FSA electronic disclosure system under the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act for annual and half-year securities reports and registration statements; API v2 needs a key; mostly Japanese.
name: EDINET

description: Japanese financial regulator that runs EDINET and sets periodic-report rules (quarterly securities reports abolished from April 2024). Local-language name(s): 金融庁.
name: Financial Services Agency (Japan)

description: Mainland China's securities regulator; sets disclosure deadlines, requires Chinese-language disclosure via appointed media, and supervises IPOs including STAR Market chip listings. Local-language name(s): 中国证监会.
name: China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC)

description: CSRC-designated information-disclosure website (www.cninfo.com.cn) carrying Chinese listed-company announcements and periodic reports; JavaScript-heavy. Local-language name(s): 巨潮资讯网.
name: CNINFO (巨潮资讯网)

description: China Association for Public Companies guideline (effective 2023-05-01) used by SSE for industry lists; 50% revenue rule; published half-yearly at major-class level only. Local-language name(s): 中国上市公司协会上市公司行业统计分类指引.
name: CAPCO listed-company industry statistical classification (2023)

description: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing's disclosure website for listed-issuer announcements, annual reports, prospectuses and Disclosure of Interests notices (DION). Local-language name(s): 披露易.
name: HKEXnews

description: Hong Kong market classification with sector 7030 Semiconductors (703010 Semiconductors; 703020 Semiconductor Equipment & Materials).
name: Hang Seng Industry Classification System (HSICS)

description: MSCI/S&P DJI Global Industry Classification Standard group for chip companies (45301020 Semiconductors; 45301010 Semiconductor Materials & Equipment); proprietary, licence-restricted.
name: GICS Industry 453010 Semiconductors & Semiconductor Equipment

description: India's exchange classification (Macro-economic sector / Sector / Industry / Basic Industry); July 2023 version has no semiconductor category.
name: NSE Indices Industry Classification Structure

description: Tel Aviv Stock Exchange disclosure site (since 2000; English since 2020) for filings of Israeli listed companies.
name: TASE MAYA

description: Dutch AFM public register holding annual and semi-annual financial reports of companies listed on EU regulated markets in the Netherlands.
name: AFM Register of Financial Reporting

description: Netherlands securities regulator receiving listed companies' financial reports under the Wft.
name: Dutch Authority for the Financial Markets (AFM)

description: US-based association of electronic component manufacturers, manufacturer representatives and authorized distributors; publishes Top-50 authorized distributor rankings and runs TrustedParts.com.
name: Electronic Components Industry Association (ECIA)

description: Berlin-based non-profit (founded 1989) of ~40 distributor and manufacturer members that collates quarterly European component-distribution resale (POS) statistics via auditor ISARTAX.
name: DMASS Europe e.V.

description: Trade association of independent (open-market) electronic component distributors; publishes IDEA-STD-1010 inspection and IDEA-QMS-9090 quality standards and certifies inspectors.
name: Independent Distributors of Electronics Association (IDEA)

description: Private US firm running a members' database of reported counterfeit/nonconforming electronic parts and high-risk suppliers; publishes an annual report on reported parts.
name: ERAI, Inc.

description: US government information-exchange program (with Canadian participation) for failure experience, suspected counterfeit and product-change/DMSMS notices among agencies and contractors.
name: Government-Industry Data Exchange Program (GIDEP)

description: Standards organisation that publishes the AS5553 and AS6081 counterfeit-parts avoidance standards (AS6081 for independent distributors).
name: SAE International

description: ECIA-run search site aggregating price and stock of genuine parts from authorized distributors only; also hosts ECIA's distributor research reports.
name: TrustedParts.com

description: Annual ECIA rankings of the top 50 authorized distributors in the Americas and worldwide (since 2021), by revenue, region, component category and end market; authorized distributors only, partly ECIA estimates.
name: ECIA Top 50 Authorized Distributors rankings

description: SAE standard (current edition 21 April 2023) on counterfeit EEE parts avoidance, detection, mitigation and disposition for independent distributors.
name: SAE AS6081A counterfeit-avoidance standard for independent distribution

description: Technology market research firm; publishes quarterly pure-foundry shares and a 'Foundry 2.0' tracker (pure-play foundries, non-memory IDMs, OSATs, photomask suppliers).
name: Counterpoint Research

description: Quarterly and annual ranking of the 10 largest foundries by revenue in USD; counts Samsung foundry business only (since c.2023), PSMC foundry services only and HuaHong Group incl. HLMC; excludes Intel Foundry's internal sales.
name: TrendForce top-10 foundry revenue ranking

description: Counterpoint quarterly and annual estimate of Foundry 2.0 revenue (foundry, non-memory IDM, OSAT, photomask & others) and company shares.
name: Counterpoint Foundry 2.0 market tracker

description: TSMC's annual estimate of the Foundry 2.0 industry (all logic wafer manufacturing incl. non-memory IDMs, packaging, testing, mask-making, others): ~US$250bn 2023, ~US$305bn 2025; TSMC share 28%/34%/40%.
name: TSMC Foundry 2.0 industry estimate

description: Corporate research lab where Lynn Conway developed the MPC multi-project chip service and co-developed the Mead-Conway VLSI methodology (1970s-1981).
name: Xerox Palo Alto Research Center (PARC)

description: Multi-project-wafer prototyping service run by USC's Information Sciences Institute since 1981 under DARPA (later DARPA/NSF) contracts; pools designs from many users onto shared fabrication runs at commercial foundries.
name: MOSIS (Metal Oxide Semiconductor Implementation Service)

description: US Department of Defense research agency; funded the VLSI program (late 1970s-1980s) and MOSIS.
name: Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA)

description: The set of SEMI equipment-communication standards (E39, E40, E87, E90, E94, E116, E148, E157 on top of SECS-II/HSMS/GEM, as defined in SEMI E192) that 300 mm fabs require for fully automated carrier, job and wafer handling.
name: SEMI GEM300 standards suite

description: SEMI E40 (process jobs: which recipe to run on which wafers) and SEMI E94 (control jobs: a unit of work for one or more carriers made of process jobs), used together for host-directed processing.
name: SEMI E40/E94 process and control job management

description: SEMI standard for host-equipment communication during carrier transfers at load ports, including carrier ID and slot-map verification.
name: SEMI E87 carrier management (CMS)

description: SEMI standard under which equipment tracks each substrate (wafer) inside the tool for the factory system.
name: SEMI E90 substrate tracking

description: SEMI standard for automatic reporting of equipment and module states, time in state and blocked reasons to the host.
name: SEMI E116 equipment performance tracking (EPT)

description: SEMI standard (first published 1986) defining six basic equipment states and reliability, availability, maintainability and utilization metrics (MTBF, MTTR, uptime).
name: SEMI E10 equipment RAM and utilization

description: SEMI standard for the hardware signals used when AMHS vehicles hand a carrier to or from a tool load port or stocker.
name: SEMI E84 carrier handoff parallel I/O

description: SEMI web-services standards suite (E120, E125, E128, E132, E134, E138, E164) for high-volume equipment data collection by multiple factory clients, alongside SECS/GEM.
name: SEMI Equipment Data Acquisition (Interface A)

description: SEMI test-data standard (first published 2021) combining a relational data container able to hold all STDF content with real-time MQTT publish-subscribe streaming for test floors.
name: SEMI E183 Rich Interactive Test Database (RITdb)

description: Automotive Electronics Council guideline for removing statistical outlier parts using static or dynamic test limits.
name: AEC-Q001 part average testing guideline

description: Body that publishes the AEC-Q qualification and screening documents used by automotive chip buyers, including AEC-Q001 on part average testing.
name: Automotive Electronics Council (AEC)

description: SEMI baseline security requirements for Windows/Linux computers in fab equipment and AMHS (OS support, network security, endpoint protection, monitoring), published 2022.
name: SEMI E187 cybersecurity of fab equipment

description: The ceiling-mounted vehicles (OHT), stockers, buffers and lifts, plus control software, that move wafer carriers (FOUPs) between tools in a fab without people carrying them.
name: Automated material handling system (AMHS)

description: Fab software that schedules and controls carrier movements by the AMHS on instruction from the MES/dispatcher.
name: Material control system (MCS)

description: Software that adjusts recipe parameters run by run from metrology and sensor data to keep process results on target.
name: Advanced process control (APC) / run-to-run system

description: Software that charts measurements against control limits and flags out-of-control conditions that stop tools and trigger action plans.
name: Statistical process control (SPC) system

description: Software that combines inline, parametric, defect, test and genealogy data to find causes of yield loss (e.g. PDF Exensio, KLA Klarity, Onto Discover, Synopsys Yield Explorer).
name: Yield management system (YMS)

description: Private network and software (owned by PDF Solutions since March 2025) through which equipment suppliers remotely monitor and, if the fab permits, control tools in customer fabs.
name: secureWISE remote equipment access network

description: MES suite from Samsung SDS covering scheduling and dispatching, manufacturing operations, material control and SECS-based tool control.
name: Samsung SDS Nexplant MES

description: Consulting and market-research firm founded in 1961; prepared the issuer-commissioned China IMSS market report used in the Glorysoft HKEX prospectus.
name: Frost & Sullivan

description: Japanese research association (founded by 15 organisations incl. Intel and Daifuku; 38 members by April 2026) developing standardised, automated back-end assembly and test lines by 2028.
name: Semiconductor Assembly Test Automation and Standardization Research Association (SATAS)
